stories.headline: WNBA playoffs 2026: Dream-Liberty live analysis, highlights
stories.summary: Las Vegas and New York look to avoid elimination in Friday's Game 3 semifinals. We're courtside for all the action.
stories.body:
The WNBA semifinals are best-of-five, but Friday marks must-win games for the Las Vegas Aces and New York Liberty, who are on the brink of elimination as they host Game 3s.

The No. 8 seed Liberty host the No. 4 Atlanta Dream (7:30 p.m. ET, ESPN2) at Barclays Center. The Dream ride a nine-game winning streak into Friday, which includes four wins over New York, dating to the last week of the regular season. Atlanta won the first two games of this semifinal series 92-82 and 101-98 in overtime.

The No. 3 seed Aces host the No. 2 Golden State Valkyries (9:30 p.m. ET) at Michelob Ultra Arena. The defending WNBA champion, Las Vegas went 3-0 against Golden State in the regular season but lost 71-60 and 83-81 in San Francisco.

Can the Liberty and Aces keep their seasons alive? Can the Dream and Valkyries complete the sweep? ESPN is courtside at both games to cover all the action. Follow along as Michael Voepel, Alexa Philippou, Kendra Andrews and Kareem Copeland check in with live updates.

stories.headline: Fantasy football Week 5 inactives: Kyle Monangai, Lamar Jackson out
stories.summary: Updated inactives and analysis based on the latest reports and official announcements leading up to kickoff.
stories.body:
Whom should you start? Whom should you sit? To help you set your fantasy football lineups and avoid starting an offensive player who won't be in the lineup, we'll post fantasy-relevant updates and analysis here as NFL teams release their official inactives lists.

Official Sunday inactives should begin coming in approximately 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff times: around 11:30 a.m. ET for the early games and 2:30 p.m. ET for the late-afternoon games.

Refresh often for the latest information.

Don't forget to check these out: Mike Clay's Playbook | Week 5 Buzz

Week 5 Rankings | Matchup rankings for Week 5

Biggest concerns heading into Week 5
Players in London
Dallas Goedert, TE, Eagles (knee): Goedert was able to return to practice this week, albeit in a limited fashion. Still, he will play in Week 5. He should operate as the top target for Jalen Hurts, especially in the red zone. Still, some names to play Goedert over this week are Brenton Strange, Dalton Schultz, and Michael Mayer.

Players with early starts
Ja'Marr Chase, WR, Bengals (concussion): Chase was able to practice this week and has a chance to suit up on Sunday. Obviously, if Chase plays, you start him. If he sits, you can look at Dohnte Meyers, who saw nine targets last week, or Mitchell Tinsley who saw seven. Mike Gesicki is also a potential "in-house" replacement option, as the Dolphins have allowed the fourth-most TE fantasy PPG.

Tee Higgins, WR, Bengals (adductor): Higgins was a DNP to start the week but returned to action in full on Friday. He is questionable for this week. Fantasy managers should have a backup plan in place, just in case. As previously stated, you could go with Meyers and Tinsley -- but, ideally, there are more trustworthy options. Some receivers you should consider starting instead this week are Carnell Tate, Romeo Doubs, and Denzel Boston.

Ashton Jeanty, RB, Raiders (ankle/foot): The Raiders star RB popped up on the injury report on Thursday after logging a limited session. He did not practice on Friday and is now questionable for Week 5. Sure, if Jeanty plays for the Raiders, he starts for your fantasy football team.

However, if he sits, Mike Washington Jr. would be a borderline RB1 play. The "floor" is less certain for Washington -- run and check to see if he's still available on the waiver wire -- but the speedy, big-play threat, brings a lot of upside. If he draws the start for Las Vegas, play him over Braelon Allen, David Montgomery, Omarion Hampton and Will Shipley.

Justin Jefferson, WR, Vikings (ankle): The star wideout returned to practice this week, and though he is questionable, he said the plan is for him to play. If Jefferson suits up, you play him in fantasy. If he sits, Jordan Addison should be viewed as a top-20 receiver.

Jordan Addison, WR, Vikings (hamstring): Addison returned to practice this week after sitting out Wednesday. He is listed as questionable but seems likely to suit up. Star wideout Justin Jefferson (ankle) is also listed as questionable, but has said the plan is for him to play. If both players suit up, Addison would be in the WR3/flex range, as a low-floor, high-upside play. If Jefferson were to sit, Addison could be viewed as a top-20 WR.

Rhamondre Stevenson, RB, Patriots (knee): Stevenson was able to log limited practice sessions this week and is questionable for Week 5. He did tell ESPN reporter Mike Reiss that he is "ready to go." If he suits up, expect the Patriots backfield to remain a split. Stevenson is the "safer floor" option, with TreVeyon Henderson being the "home run hitting" play. Both are in the flex range. If he were to sit, Henderson becomes a must start.

Alvin Kamara, RB, Saints: Kamara is being listed as questionable, even though he was able to practice this week and seems likely to play. He should once again operate as the Saints' lead back. While he needs catches and touchdowns to make up for his inefficiency, volume has him in play as an RB3/flex option.

Cam Skattebo, RB, Giants (shoulder): Skattebo was limited at practice, wearing a red noncontact jersey to start the week. Still, he appears to be good to go heading into Sunday. Skattebo is one of the safest bets for volume each week and should be started as an RB2, even in a tough matchup on paper. Plus, with bad weather potentially in the forecast, he could even see an uptick in usage.

Isaiah Likely, TE, Giants (knee/groin): Likely was limited to start the week but does not carry an injury designation heading in Week 5. Likely has seen a 33% target share with Jameis Winston under center. That duo is coming off their best game together. Plus, the Commanders have allowed the most passing touchdowns in the league. It's a good setup for Likely, who is the Giants' top red zone option. He should be started with confidence.

Malik Nabers, WR, Giants (knee): Nabers sat out Wednesday's practice due to soreness in his knee, but will play in Week 5. This seems like something fantasy managers need to get used to, as mid-week rest days could become a frequent sight this season. Nabers is coming off his best game of the season and should comfortably be started this week.

Rico Dowdle, RB, Steelers (toe): Dowdle has been limited at practice this week and is questionable for Week 5. Still, practicing all week puts him on pace to return. Jaylen Warren has thrived with Dowdle sidelined and I would expect him to continue to operate in the lead-back role. While Dowdle will be involved, Warren remains a top-15 RB play this week. Dowdle is someone who should be benched in fantasy until we have more clarity on his role. However, check for him on your league's waiver wire as he was dropped by a fair amount of fantasy teams over the past two weeks.

Carnell Tate, WR, Titans (back): Tate was added to the injury report on Thursday, which caused a scare in the fantasy community. However, he is good to go for Week 5 and should be started. He has seen his target rate continuously climb, reaching 43% in Week 4. Not only that, but 26 out of his 32 targets have come against zone coverage, which the Texans have played on 83% of their plays. Lastly, the Texans are top two in both yards and touchdowns allowed to receivers.

Jayden Daniels, QB, Commanders (elbow): Daniels has been practicing with a brace on his left elbow and will play in Week 5. While there is some added risk to be found here, fantasy managers should look to get Daniels back into their starting lineups. Even if the Commanders have less designed runs for their star QB, the upside is too high to get away from. Daniels is a top-5 QB option in Week 5.

Jacory Croskey-Merritt, RB, Commanders (groin): JCM joins seemingly all of his teammates on the injury report this week. He has been limited this week but is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 5. The Giants have allowed 99 RB rushing yards per game and allow explosive runs at the third-highest rate (12.5%). With Daniels coming off of his injury, do not be surprised if the Commanders run more than usual. Plus, game script could be on his side. Croskey-Merritt is a high-upside flex option.

Rachaad White, RB, Commanders (shoulder): After missing Week 4, White has been able to return to the practice field. He is expected to play on Sunday. That likely puts some restraints on JCM's fantasy value. Still, Croskey-Merritt is the preferred option of the two Commanders backs. Consider both to be flex options in a favorable matchup.

Terry McLaurin WR, Commanders (hamstring): McLaurin was able to log a limited session Friday and is expected to play Sunday. Even if he can go, he is a riskier option than normal, as hamstrings are always at risk of flaring up. He would be more of a flex option than his usual WR2 status. With Stefon Diggs not playing, the Commanders could be thin at receiver this week. Antonio Williams (eight targets last week) would be a sleeper flex option, likely operating as the top Commanders target. Chig Okonkwo, who was limited at practice this week but will play, would be a sleeper tight end for those in need of a streaming option.

-->
Players with late starts

Ladd McConkey, WR, Chargers (foot): McConkey has not practiced this week and is on the wrong side of questionable heading into Week 5. If McConkey sits, Tre' Harris and Oronde Gadsden could see a bump in volume. That said, even with the Broncos potentially playing without their top two CBs, I would look to completely avoid the Chargers offense.

Players on Sunday night
Zay Flowers, WR, Ravens (foot): Flowers has been no stranger to the injury report this week. He has practiced all week in a limited fashion and is questionable for Week 5. While he seems likely to play, it would not be a bad idea for fantasy managers to have a pivot option just in case. His fantasy value takes a hit without Lamar Jackson, but Flowers is still in play as a WR3 or flex option. In 10 career games with Tyler Huntley he has averaged six targets, 4.6 catches and 66 yards per game. He scored four touchdowns in those games.

Players on Monday night
DJ Moore, WR, Bills (shoulder): Moore missed practice to start the week. This has been a recent trend from him, but he always seems able to suit up. Still, he seems up in the air heading into Monday night. Even if he can play, the bigger problem is that he has had to leave the game early twice in the last three weeks. That makes it difficult to trust him.

If you have any other option you feel good about -- for instance I am sitting him for Nabers in one league and Christian Watson/Parker Washington in another -- I say you take it. If you do roll the dice on Moore, make sure to have an insurance policy in place since the game is on Monday night. Keon Coleman would be the top option, but Khalil Shakir is another.

Ruled out before Sunday
Lamar Jackson, QB, Ravens (ankle): The two-time MVP had his ankle rolled up last week and is in jeopardy of missing a couple of games. It's unfortunate because Jackson has been playing at a very high level. He's working a career high in yards per attempt (10.1) and completion percentage (70.8%), while averaging 58 rushing yards per game. With him out, Huntley will start for the Ravens, but he's more suited for superflex leagues. Some streaming options this week for managers in need are Jacoby Brissett, Jameis Winston and Aaron Rodgers.

Kyle Monangai, RB, Bears (thumb/toe): Monangai will be out for Week 5. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler has reported that Monangai is dealing with "turf toe" and could possibly even miss another week or two. D'Andre Swift continues to deal with a knee injury. Although he has not missed any time due to his injury, his fumbling woes have caused his coach some concerns. Swift should see even more volume and is a must-start fantasy RB1 with Monangai out.

Pat Surtain II, CB, Broncos (ankle): Neither Surtain nor Riley Moss have practiced this week and both are out for Week 5. That would certainly make life easier for all Chargers pass catchers, if you're into that sort of thing.

Rashawn Slater, OT, Chargers (ankle): The Chargers tackle is expected to be sidelined for four-to-six weeks due to a high ankle sprain. This just makes it tougher to trust Justin Herbert and Omarion Hampton. I would look to avoid both of those players against a tough Broncos defense. Additionally, OT Joe Alt suffered a neck injury and has not practiced this week. It's very tough to trust any Chargers this week.

Quentin Johnston, WR, Chargers (chest): The Chargers receiver is out for Week 5 against the Broncos. That should lead to a bump for Harris and the other available Chargers pass catchers. Still, given their offensive woes and O-line injuries, the Chargers should be avoided by fantasy managers this week.

Mack Hollins, WR, Patriots (calf): Hollins has not practiced this week and has been ruled out for Week 5 That would makes Romeo Doubs, who had nine targets last week, even more appealing. Doubs should be started over Deebo Samuel Sr., Roman Wilson, KC Concepcion, and Courtland Sutton.

Saquon Barkley, RB, Eagles (hamstring): Barkley exited last week's game and is out for Week 5 due to a hamstring injury. The Eagles also placed RB Tank Bigsby on IR this week, leaving Will Shipley as their lead back. Fantasy managers may need to use Shipley this week, but should look to avoid him if possible. He faces the Jaguars, a team that has allowed the fewest RB rushing yards per game -- and just one rushing touchdown all season.

DeVonta Smith, WR, Eagles (hamstring): Smith is out heading into the Eagles' London matchup against the Jaguars. That leaves Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon as the team's top receivers. Still, no Eagles pass catcher reached as many as 35 yards last week and the team will now be operating without two expected starters on their offensive line. While one could opt to simply pivot to Dallas Goedert, it's probably best to seek options elsewhere to replace Smith.

Michael Pittman Jr, WR, Steelers (foot): Pittman has aggravated a foot injury and will miss multiple weeks. He had been off to a slow start, so fantasy managers should have already been looking in another direction. This means more run for Roman Wilson, who has become a Rodgers favorite of late. Wilson is a deep-league flex option in a favorable matchup.

Stefon Diggs, WR, Commanders (hamstring): Diggs, who saw nine targets last week, did not practice this week due to a hamstring injury that will keep him out for Week 5. With Terry McLaurin also up in the air, the Commanders are suddenly looking very thin at receiver. Antonio Williams (who saw eight targets last week) would be a sleeper flex option, likely operating as the top Commanders target. Chig Okonkwo, who was limited at practice this week but appears likely to play, would be a sleeper tight end for those in need of a streaming option.

stories.headline: Roberto De Zerbi: Dejan Kulusevski return can inspire Spurs at Man United
stories.summary: Roberto De Zerbi has urged winless Tottenham to draw inspiration from Dejan Kulusevski's comeback ahead of Saturday's trip to Manchester United.
stories.body:
Roberto De Zerbi has urged winless Tottenham to draw inspiration from Dejan Kulusevski's comeback ahead of Saturday's trip to Manchester United.

Kulusevski has not played for Spurs in more than 500 days following a serious knee injury, but featured in a behind-closed-doors match during the international break and will travel to Old Trafford to offer support.

With Kulusevski inching closer to an emotional return after multiple setbacks and fears he may never play again, De Zerbi used the Swedish attacker as a reference point for bottom-of-the-table Tottenham, who have taken two points from their first five Premier League fixtures.

"Yes, he's an inspiration," De Zerbi said. "He reacted very well, with character, with courage, with passion. Yes, passion. It's a good word, passion. We have to take inspiration from Deki. I said the same in the meeting to the players.

"[Away at Old Trafford] he comes with us, also [Pedro] Porro [for support]. I want all players tonight and tomorrow, but he is working very well. I think he is an example for everyone, Dejan Kulusevski.

"Forget the player, but the example of how he reacted to the injury, the reaction to being unlucky, the character he showed this time, was an example, a reference for everyone."

Quizzed on when he could make his long-awaited return, De Zerbi explained: "I don't know, it's not just my responsibility.

"We are working together with the medical staff. They are working very well with him, they have done special work. We have to analyse week by week."

Spurs have sorely missed the creativity and character of Kulusevski during his 17-month absence, but De Zerbi is calm after a slow start to the campaign and was reminded of a similar situation for Aston Villa last season.

Asked about Villa being able to finish fourth after they went five games without a win, De Zerbi said: "Yes, it's possible. Why not? But to do what Villa did, we have to click.

"I think the first win is not a gift from God. You have to deserve to win. And we didn't deserve to win so far."

James Maddison will travel to Old Trafford and is available but De Zerbi hinted he might only have a cameo role after he missed days of training over the last week.

With Kulusevski still absent and Maddison not back to his best, it has increased calls for Spurs' highly rated 18-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett to get an opportunity.

Major clubs across the world are circling playmaker Williams-Barnett, but Spurs have opened talks with the mercurial talent over a new deal, the Press Association reported.

De Zerbi acknowledged he was "thinking" about when to include Williams-Barnett in the squad after he made his second Tottenham appearance late on in the Carabao Cup win over Charlton.

"Special talent, special personality also because he's arrogant, but arrogant good for football," De Zerbi said of Williams-Barnett.

"You have to believe in yourself. Not forgetting to be humble. Anyway, humility but believe in yourself and the right example is Luca."

stories.headline: Guardians' Williams, White Sox's Burke to start for ALCS bid
stories.summary: After finishing Game 4 of the ALDS on the mound, Guardians right-hander Gavin Williams will get the ball to start Game 5, while the White Sox will go with righty Sean Burke.
stories.body:
After finishing Game 4 of the American League Division Series on the mound, Cleveland Guardians right-hander Gavin Williams will get the ball to start Game 5 on Saturday, manager Stephen Vogt announced.

Williams, 27, thew 18 pitches in relief of Cade Smith on Thursday as the Chicago White Sox were mounting a comeback against the Guardians' closer. But Williams was able to secure the victory, forcing a winner-take-all game.

"We're hoping [Thursday] acts as a higher-intensity bullpen," Vogt said Friday of Williams' Game 4 outing. "So Gavin is ready to go tomorrow. Feels good today. So we will obviously see how he's doing tomorrow."

Williams started Game 2 of the series, throwing 98 pitches over five innings. He will be opposed by Chicago right-hander Sean Burke, who would have entered Game 4 if his team had tied the game in the ninth inning. Burke also appeared in Game 2, pitching 5⅓ innings after the White Sox used an opener.

That won't be the case in Game 5. It's Burke's ball to start the night.

"We talked a little bit about some of the exposure to different parts of the lineup that are a factor," Chicago manager Will Venable said. "Just kind of looking at who we have and who we're going to use tomorrow and how we can transition from one guy to the other."

Both bullpens are taxed. Smith pitched in Games 3 and 4 despite the Guardians holding big leads in both contests. He struggled in his fourth inning over the two outings, prompting questions about his usage.

"If anybody thinks it's easy, go ahead," Vogt said with a smirk. "It's really difficult.

"I think when you're playing a team that's got the offensive power that they do and as you're managing a bullpen, you always go to worst-case scenario in your head. ... We all put our heads together, and all signs pointed to let's put Cade in this thing and let's stop it right here."

It didn't work, and now Smith's availability for Game 5 is in question. He has appeared in every game of the series, though off days have helped in his recovery.

"We're going to talk to him tomorrow and see how he feels," Vogt said. "I don't know if it's something that we can push to a ton of pitches tomorrow."

The White Sox might be in a similar position with right-hander Grant Taylor after he was tagged for four runs without recording an out in Game 4. He has thrown 67 pitches in three ALDS outings.

Scoring has increased throughout the series as hitters on both teams are facing tired arms with increased familiarity. The winner will take on the Tampa Bay Rays in the AL Championship Series, which begins Monday.

"At the end of the day, Game 5, deciding game here of a series, it's going to be all hands on deck," Venable said. "You kind of throw out the window, previous usage. You obviously want to be in tune with the guys and how they're feeling, but I think Stephen would say the same thing. We're going for it here."

stories.headline: Miami coach urges MLS fans to enjoy Lionel Messi after Argentina adiós
stories.summary: Inter Miami coach Cristian "Kily" González said Argentina will miss Lionel Messi following the captain's international retirement before urging fans to enjoy his time with the MLS club.
stories.body:
Inter Miami head coach Cristian "Kily" González said Argentina will miss Lionel Messi terribly following the captain's international retirement before urging fans to enjoy his time with the MLS club.

"[The farewell match] was incredibly intense," González said on Friday. "Obviously, I was very close to him, but ultimately, that moment belonged to him, it was his time.

"All that mattered was for him to enjoy it. I just told him to enjoy it, to soak up all the love, not just from Argentina, but from the whole world.

"He'll be missed in that jersey, of course, but today we have him here, and we have to enjoy having him with us now.

"He's going to miss it, from the day he retires until the day he's no longer around. I have no doubt that, for him, the national team was all about wearing that jersey; he'll always miss the mark he left and the legacy he created there. But unfortunately, we won't see him in that jersey anymore, so those of us here have to enjoy it. Now he's ours, so I have to enjoy it."

González added that Messi left a lasting legacy with Argentina due to his competitive nature, inspiring those around him to improve every day.

"Leo is someone who conveys a certain mindset every day; he demands that his teammates, and all of us, give 100% in every respect," González said.

"He's a born competitor. You see it in every training session, and it's incredible. He's 39 years old, yet he's constantly seeking out new challenges. That's fantastic for everyone, not just his teammates, but the staff and the club as well.

"He pushes you to be better every single day.

"That's why he's such an example; as I said before, he'll be missed on the national team because he left a legacy there, and he's leaving a legacy here too, the club changed the day he arrived.

"He drives us to improve daily and to be prepared in every way. And he's happy, I see him enjoying himself, and that makes me very happy, too."

Messi and Inter Miami now prepare to face D.C. United on Saturday night at Nu Stadium in the first game back after the international break.

"We're in a good place. The guys who returned from their respective national teams are doing really well," González said. "We've trained effectively, and we know we need to get back to winning, that's a given. We have a few matches to settle in properly, reach the final stretch of the season in top form, and fine-tune the details so we can be the best team possible."

Inter Miami currently sits in third place on the Eastern Conference table with 46 points in 27 games following a five-match winless streak in MLS. The Herons recorded one loss and four draws in their last five regular-season MLS games.

Inter Miami did, however, defeat Cruz Azul 2-0 in the Campeones Cup on Sept. 16.

"We have a very clear idea of what we want and what we're aiming for. Defensively, we need to be much better; we're facing an opponent that relies heavily on transitions and is very dangerous in those situations, so we have to guard against that.

"At the same time, we can't lose sight of the fact that we need to take the initiative and go out to win the match. As I just said, we need to get back to winning ways, and hopefully, we can achieve that."

Inter Miami will then host New York City FC on Oct. 14 at Nu Stadium.

stories.headline: Panthers eyeing six-week timeline for Brad Marchand's return
stories.summary: The Panthers are expecting forward Brad Marchand to miss about six weeks with his left leg injury, a timeline that coincides with Aleksander Barkov being out six to eight weeks.
stories.body:
The Florida Panthers are expecting forward Brad Marchand to miss about six weeks with his left leg injury, coach Paul Maurice told reporters Friday.

The timeline coincides closely to that of Aleksander Barkov, as Maurice announced earlier this week that Barkov won't require surgery on his left leg injury and is expected to be available again within six to eight weeks.

Marchand, who didn't play in the team's first two games, suffered his injury during a 2-1 win over the Los Angeles Kings on Tuesday as the Panthers wrapped up a season-opening four-game road trip.

He was hurt after taking a stick to the face from Kings defenseman Brandt Clarke with 52.6 seconds remaining, causing him to twist around and collide with the right post before his left leg bent back in awkwardly.

Marchand was down on the ice for several minutes being examined by an athletic trainer before teammates Brady Tkachuk and Niko Mikkola helped him to the bench, with Marchand unable to put weight on his leg. He was then helped back to the dressing room.

Florida won back-to-back Stanley Cup titles in 2024 and 2025 but missed the playoffs last season after a slew of players -- Barkov and Marchand among them -- were derailed by injuries.

On Thursday, Barkov called his diagnosis "really good news" and said he planned to meet with the Panthers as early as Friday to develop a concise return-to-play plan, including setting a target for when he can resume skating.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Singapore Grand Prix: FIA confirms software issue in sprint qualifying was caused by 'human error'
stories.summary: Formula 1 encountered its second technical mishap in a less than a week after an FIA official forgot to push a button needed to enable full engine power in sprint qualifying for the Singapore Grand Prix.
stories.body:
SINGAPORE -- Formula 1 encountered its second technical mishap in a less than a week after an FIA official forgot to push a button needed to enable full engine power in sprint qualifying for the Singapore Grand Prix.

Qualifying was red-flagged in SQ1, the first elimination session, due to debris from Sergio Pérez's Cadillac, which automatically suspended the extra amount of "overtake mode" power delivered to engines on safety grounds.

That mode can be reactivated only manually by an FIA official from race control when the session resumes as normal. However, that did not happen initially when SQ1 resumed and cars returned to the racetrack to complete the session.

The FIA was soon notified via driver and team feedback that this had not been done when the session got back underway.

The power mode was then turned on for 27 seconds, only to be turned off again when the FIA race control expressed a concern over sporting fairness, although those two decisions affected drivers differently depending on where they were on the racetrack during timed runs.

One of those was Williams driver Carlos Sainz, who was eliminated in SQ1.

"Half of the cars did the lap with half a second quicker engine than the others," Sainz said Friday. "There was another software issue with the cars, this time around we were on the bad end of it."

Also eliminated alongside Sainz in SQ1 was Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad, Aston Martin's Lance Stroll, Williams' Alex Albon and Sainz, and Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas and Pérez.

The FIA later released a statement confirming "a human error in Race Control unrelated to the timing issue also encountered in SQ1."

The statement added: "When it became apparent that Overtake Mode was not active after the restart, it was then activated for a period of 27 seconds before being deactivated again. The FIA acknowledges that this unfortunate human error had an impact on the performance of certain cars based on the timing of their run and their position around the lap. The second and third periods of Sprint Qualifying were not affected."

The session set the grid for a sprint race Saturday afternoon.

Next steps are unclear, although teams affected are free to protest the outcome of the session.

It's unclear what the stewards would do if they found a protest admissible.

In theory, ​stewards could declare the qualifying result void, but there is no precedent for what would happen in that instance and how the grid would be set as a result.

It is the second engine-related embarrassment for the sport in a week.

- When can Kimi Antonelli win the F1 title? Earliest date, points needed and remaining races

- Max Verstappen takes first pole for sprint race at Singapore Grand Prix following another settings issue

- 'Watch Teletubbies, not F1': Toto Wolff hits back at 'brainless' Kimi Antonelli driver favoritism claims

Sunday's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia was red-flagged when a software glitch saw cars across the field lose power in their hybrid V6 engines during a formation lap.

The FIA was only able to restart the race 48 minutes after the first issue became apparent when it recoded a software upgrade that every team used to update its engines.

Drivers called the Bahrain issue "horrible" and "totally unacceptable."

On this occasion, there are more headaches for the FIA.

Sainz questioned why Singapore's sprint qualifying session was allowed to finish in the first place when last week the FIA stopped the formation lap on the spot as soon as an issue was detected.

"For whatever reason the FIA, [un]like in Malaysia, they didn't decide to do sporting equity and were happy to do half of the cars in quali[fying] with higher power than the other half of the cars," he said. "A bit confused why the sport keeps doing different things based on who is out in Q1 and who is out in Lap 1."

Sainz's comment referred to the controversy that followed last weekend's aborted start.

The FIA had effectively red-flagged the formation lap as cars lost power at different points.

Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso questioned afterward why the FIA had aborted the start when some cars were still going and others had stopped or slowed significantly.

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, who had started second, had been passed by half the field when his car ground to a near standstill, although he got going again as the FIA aborted the formation lap.

The race was then controversially restarted with the grid unchanged, meaning Hamilton kept his spot on the front row and others who had dropped down the order started as if nothing had happened.

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little earlier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Friday, Oct. 9
Butters is a Bulldog

Zak Butters is officially a Western Bulldog. Port Adelaide will not match the offer and accept pick No. 5 as compensation, having also earlier secured picks 6, 10, and two future-firsts in the five-club mega trade. The star free agent and three-time All-Australian, who played 156 games and kicked 73 goals for the Power after being drafted in 2019, has signed a nine-year deal with his boyhood club

Hawks land spearhead King

After securing Zach Merrett earlier this week, Hawthorn have officially welcomed Ben King today after gold Coast elected not to match the offer for the restricted free agent. the Suns will receive a first round pick as compensation, which currently stands at pick No. 7.

Mega trade approved

The league approved a mega trade involving Port Adelaide, the Bulldogs, Melbourne, Hawthorn and Carlton, two players and scores of picks.

Under the five-team deal, the Bulldogs gave up picks No.12 and No.31 and a 2028 first-rounder to bring in Hawthorn's Finn Maginness, Carlton's Hudson O'Keeffe and later picks in this year's draft and future years.

Port parted with picks No.4, 46 and 81 and six second-round or worse future selections to get back picks No.6 and No.10, Melbourne's 2027 first-rounder and the Dogs' 2028 first-rounder.

The Demons surrendered picks No.6, 10 and 87 and their 2027 first-rounder -- as well as two late future picks -- for picks No.4, 12, 31 and 46.

Hawthorn (2027 third-rounder) and Carlton (2028 fourth-rounder) received late future picks for Maginness and O'Keeffe.

-- AAP

Flag Lion gets his wish

Brisbane has traded second-year Lion and 2025 premiership player Sam Marshall and pick No.39 to St Kilda for a 2027 first-rounder.

Thursday, Oct. 8
Marshall lands at the Cats

St Kilda have pulled the trigger on a deal to send contracted ruckman Rowan Marshall to Geelong, as the Cats and other rival clubs circle Sydney star Nick Blakey.

Geelong traded pick No.14 in this year's draft for the disenchanted 30-year-old and a third-round selection in 2028 on Thursday afternoon.

New Zealand-born Marshall had requested a move to the Cats for a second straight year after St Kilda recruited Tom De Koning to become their first-choice ruckman.

-- AAP

Wednesday, Oct. 7
Dons defender gets traded to the Cats

After being denied a trade last year, Jordan Ridley got his wish for a fresh start after Essendon and Geelong agreed to a deal on Wednesday.

Geelong gave up utility Jack Bowes, a 2027 first-round pick and 2028 second-round pick to get the 27-year-old Ridley through the door.

Pick No. 60 and a 2028 fourth-round selection will come back to the Cats from the Bombers.

--AAP

Tuesday, Oct. 6
O'Driscoll makes the move over east

Fremantle have traded 24-year-old Nathan O'Driscoll to Richmond in exchange for pick 61 in this year's draft.

The winger played 17 games for the Dockers this season but wasn't selected for the Grand Final.

Monday, Oct. 5
TRADE PERIOD OPENS
Merrett finally becomes a Hawk

After attempting to join Hawthorn last year, Zach Merrett has finally been traded from Essendon to the Hawks.

Hawthorn have sent picks 15, 25 and a 2028 second-round pick in exchange for the 31-year-old.

Merrett leaves the Bombers a week after winning a record-equaling seventh Crichton Medal, three All-Australian blazers, and 274 games.

Pendlebury becomes a Sun

AFL games record holder Scott Pendlebury is officially a Sun after Gold Coast and Collingwood agreed on a trade for the 38-year-old veteran.

Pendlebury, a two-time premiership player, heads to the Suns in exchange for pick No. 65 in this year's draft.

"It's an exciting group here at the SUNS and the opportunity to bring a few different ideas and also learn from a great group of coaches and players is one I'm really looking forward to," Pendlebury told the Suns.

"This side is one I've watched from afar and really admired. I've got a bit of knowledge about the industry so I'm here to play my role and help this squad continue to develop."

Jesse Hogan traded from GWS to Collingwood

Out-of-favour Giants forward Jesse Hogan has made the switch to Collingwood in exchange for pick 75.

The 31-year-old won the Coleman Medal in 2024 but has been unable to recapture his best form at the Giants in the two years since.

Magpies list boss Justin Leppitsch said Hogan would be a valuable addition.

"On behalf of everyone at Collingwood, I'd like to warmly welcome Jesse to Collingwood. Jesse has established himself as one of the competition's premier key forwards and we're excited to see him bring his experience and talent to our club," he said.

"His aerial presence inside forward-50 and his consistency as a goal-kicker make him a genuine threat.

"Like Lachie (Neale), Jesse has a passion to teach the next generation and will make a great addition to our club."

Saturday, Oct. 3
Bulldogs seal free-agency signing of key defender

The Western Bulldogs have finally snagged the key defender they need, securing Adelaide backman Jordon Butts as an unrestricted free agent.

The Bulldogs are set for a bumper AFL trade period headlined by working through a deal for Port Adelaide superstar Zak Butters, ahead of a 2027 season where the club will have high expectations.

But after seeing off Carlton's advances to keep hold of defender Buku Khamis, the Bulldogs have filled a major area of need by adding 26-year-old Butts.

Adelaide will receive a second-round compensation selection, currently pick No.33, in this year's draft.

-- AAP

Friday, Oct. 2
FREE AGENCY OPEN
Three-peat Lion locks in Magpies move

Lachie Neale has sealed his high-profile switch to Collingwood, with Brisbane teasing the dual Brownlow medallist on his way out the door.

The AFL approved Neale signing a three-year deal with the Magpies on Friday afternoon, closing out the first day of free agency.

The 33-year-old ball-winner leaves as an unrestricted free agent after the Lions clinched a third straight flag with their stunning seven-point grand final victory over Fremantle.

-- AAP

Greene on his way to the Cats

Toby Greene will join Geelong as an unrestricted free agent on a three-year deal, re-partnering with former Giants teammate Jeremey Cameron.

The paperwork was lodged to the AFL on Friday morning.

The Giants receive band three compensation for Greene, which is currently pick No. 26 in the upcoming draft.

Greene departs the Giants with his name etched in the club's record books, sitting first in games played for the club with a tally of 282 games, as well as leading the club's all-time goalkicking tally with 450 majors.

Briggs now a Tiger

Richmond has landed GWS ruck Kieren Briggs as an unrestricted free agent.

Briggs' move to the Tigers was confirmed just hours after the free agency window opened on Friday.

Briggs played 88 games for GWS after joining the club as the No.34 pick in the 2018 draft.

Amartey officially joins the Blues

Free agency has opened with a bang, with out-of-favour key forward Joel Amartey committing to Carlton.

Details are still to come on the length of contract, and Sydney's compensation.

Hawthorn father-son recommits despite interest

Calsher Dear has made a shock decision to re-sign with the Hawks for two years, despite being out of favour thorughout 2026.

The 20-year-old has kicked 39 goals from 31 games, but found himself behind Jack Gunston, Mitch Lewis and Mabior Chol. With Gunston signed on and Suns forward Ben King expected to sign with the Hawks as well, there were questions about whether Dear would get enough opportunity at his childhood club.

Hawks list boss Mark McKenzie said the club was "really pleased" that Dear had recommitted.

"He remains an important part of what we are trying to achieve as a club," he said.

"Following his debut season, Calsher showed us all the special talent that he is, but as a key tall at 21 years of age, we've needed to be patient with his progression.

"Having battled several injuries over his first three seasons in the system, we are very excited about what the future holds for Calsher with a strong pre-season under his belt and greater continuity into 2027 and beyond."

Thursday, Oct. 1
Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: Jake Paul cleared to fight; Canelo, Strickland, others on wish list
stories.summary: Jake Paul, who has been cleared to resume fighting after recovering from a broken jaw, has a list of big names he'd like to face in boxing and MMA now that he's back.
stories.body:
Jake Paul has been medically cleared to return to boxing.

Paul (12-2, seven KOs), 29, has not fought since he suffered a broken jaw during his knockout loss to Anthony Joshua last December. Paul underwent surgical procedures on his jaw in December and February. Nakisa Bidarian, co-founder of Paul's Most Valuable Promotions, officially updated Paul's status Thursday.

"Jake Paul has been cleared to return to the boxing ring," Bidarian wrote on X.

Paul told ESPN in April that he'd resumed light training but had not been cleared to spar. He has targeted a full return to competition in early 2027.

In connection to the update on his health, Paul provided his latest wish list of eventual fights this week. The list included 15 potential fights, including Canelo Alvarez, Ryan Garcia, Francis Ngannou, Deontay Wilder in boxing as well as mixed martial arts contests against Conor McGregor and Nate Diaz.

The list also included UFC middleweight champion Sean Strickland (31-7), who linked himself to Paul this week in a series of online posts expressing frustration about his UFC contract.

"I gotta be honest, unless things change with the UFC I'm kinda over it," Strickland wrote on X. "McGregor makes 30 million to fight for 30 seconds and they don't want to pay us a fraction of it. Contemplating just going to 205 [pounds], knocking out my contract and scrapping with [Jake Paul]. That sounds fun."

Paul, who has been vocal for years along with MVP in encouraging the UFC to increase its fighter pay, acknowledged Strickland's post in a response.

"Sean Strickland I see your texts but are you out of contract?" Paul wrote. "Tell your 'promoter' to call MVP."

stories.headline: Mikel Arteta: 'I still have the scar' from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat
stories.summary: Mikel Arteta has said he still has a "scar" from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in May.
stories.body:
Mikel Arteta has said he still has a "scar" from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in May.

The Spaniard, whose new four-year contract at the Emirates was announced on Wednesday, took the club to their first Champions League final for 20 years last season but saw his team defeated on penalties after a 1-1 draw.

Echoing the words of the last man to take them to the brink of elite European glory -- Arsène Wenger, who previously said that "every defeat is a scar in your heart" -- Arteta told The Athletic: "I still have the scar, like Arsène says.

"I still have that poison in my veins. It has to stay there because that's when you learn and that probably is going to be a massive driver for me and everybody."

Looking towards the future, Arteta added that he was excited for a number of different aspects of the club's growth.

"Globally, with our supporters? Great. How are we going to build the next three squads? Great. How the rules of the game are going to change us, and how we're going to stay ahead of that to take advantage? Great," he said.

"But this is going to happen if every single day we look after what we built. We make it a little bit better, like software that is upgrading and upgrading. When can it stop is infinite."

He added: "It feels like it's still a lot to do, and it's just the beginning."

Arteta has, however, already managed to do something no Arsenal manager had achieved for 22 years: win a league title.

"It wasn't just a trophy. It was a moment that we're going to remember for the rest of our lives," he said.

Asked what game from his Arsenal tenure he would relive, the 44-year-old chose the controversial 1-0 win over West Ham which put the Gunners on the brink of returning to the top of the perch.

"This is football elevated to its best version, when a journey, a moment that can change so many people's lives, goes one way or the other," he said. "You just pray because you know if it goes the wrong side, probably it's gone again.

"That day when I went home, I said, 'We're going to be champions. It is our year. This has happened for a reason, and we're going to get it done.'"

Arsenal return from the international break in Saturday's early kickoff against Leeds United at the Emirates, looking to return to the top of the table ahead of Manchester City's trip to Liverpool on Sunday.

stories.headline: NRL: Spencer Leniu signs with Eels after early Roosters release
stories.summary: Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.
stories.body:
Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.

Leniu finished his three-year stint at the Tricolours on a high after a stellar performance in their 19-18 win over Newcastle to secure the 2026 trophy.

The NSW Origin representative added the Roosters' premiership ring to the three he won with Penrith from 2021-2023.

Leniu was granted a release from the final year of his Roosters contract, which will give the club some salary cap reprieve

The hard-hitting forward's Eels contract is reportedly worth more than the $850,000 per year he was making with Easts, where he spent much of his time coming off the bench.

He is expected to play a more active role in blue and gold, leading the line for the Eels' forward pack.

The westward move will see the former Panther reunite with good friend Jarome Luai, but first the pair will both suit up for Toa Samoa at the Rugby League World Cup.

Eels general manager of football Mark O'Neill shared his delight at signing one of the game's "premier enforcers".

"We're thrilled to have Spencer join the Parramatta Eels and become part of what we're building at this club," O'Neill said in a statement.

"He's one of the elite middle forwards in the game and has consistently performed on the biggest stages throughout his career.

The exit of Leniu adds to the exodus of stars from the Roosters premiership lineup.

Angus Crichton and Mark Nawaqanitawase are rugby-bound, Daly Cherry-Evans is joining Hull FC, while Daniel Tupou retired this week after his 307-game career.

Connor Watson, who missed the title decider due to concussion, has signed for a season with St George Illawarra Dragons.

Roosters coach Trent Robinson said Leniu had been a strong contributor during his time at the club.

"Spencer has brought a lot to our group over the last three years, both through the way he plays and the energy and personality he brings every day," Robinson said in a statement on Thursday.

"He brings an intensity and competitiveness to everything he does, and he challenges the people around him to be better.

"To see him finish his time here as a premiership winner is something he should be really proud of, and something we'll always share together."

With his departure announced at the Roosters' awards night on Wednesday, Leniu said he would leave the club on a high.

""I'm proud to have worn the Roosters jersey and I'll always have a lot of love and respect for the club, the boys and everyone who has supported me during my time here," said Leniu.

"Winning a premiership with this group and sharing that with the boys, our families and everyone at the club is something I'll carry with me for the rest of my life."

stories.headline: Fantasy playbook: NFL Week 5 Shadow Reports, lineup locks and projected scores
stories.summary: An all-encompassing look at the matchups to exploit or avoid and lineup locks in fantasy, as well as projected scores for all NFL games.
stories.body:
Welcome to The Playbook for Week 5, which kicked off Thursday night with a game between the Buccaneers and Cowboys.

This column features score projections, over/unders, win probabilities, and of course, easily digestible fantasy advice for seasonlong leagues and DFS. This guide should help you with all sorts of decision-making, including sit/start, last-minute waiver adds and lineup choices.

Additionally, we have folded our Shadow Reports into the game-by-game breakdowns here. Using our play-by-play data, we're able to identify defensive schemes and where each wide receiver and cornerback lines up on each play. By tracking these WR/CB matchups, including potential shadow situations, we can offer the best fantasy guidance each week.

If you want a more detailed look at some of this data, be sure to check out the weekly Shadow Reports: WR vs. CB Cheat Sheet. You can also take a look at the analysis of each team's strength of schedule for the remainder of the season.

All of this advice is centered on 12-team PPR leagues with relatively standard scoring and lineup settings (1 QB, 2 RB, 3 WR, 1 Flex, 1 K, 1 D/ST), although I'll often mention "shallow" or "deep" leagues for some starters. The charts show all players who have been projected for at least 6.0 fantasy points this week, as well as all D/STs. "Matchup" is automatically determined using a proprietary metric that factors in raw and volume-adjusted fantasy points allowed to each position by the opposing defense.

DFS values in the charts below (and their relative quality) are provided only for Sunday's main slate, which is why there are no values for games scheduled on days other than Sunday.

(Editor's note: Projections and rankings will align almost perfectly, but sometimes when a projection is close, a player might be ranked slightly higher or lower because of other factors, including upside or risk. This column is subject to updates during the weekend, although at the very minimum, rankings will be updated on the site and projections will always be updated inside the game leading up to kickoff.)

PHI-JAX | CHI-GB | HOU-TEN | CIN-MIA | LV-NE | MIN-NO | CLE-NYJ

IND-PIT | NYG-WAS | DEN-LAC | DET-ARI | SF-SEA | BAL-ATL | BUF-LAR

Tampa Bay Buccaneers @ Dallas Cowboys
Projected score: Cowboys 29, Buccaneers 19

Lineup locks: Javonte Williams, Bucky Irving, CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens

Fantasy scoop: Jalon Daniels made his first NFL start last week against Green Bay, and it did not go particularly well for the Tampa Bay offense. Daniels completed 19 out of 27 passes for 148 yards, one TD and two INTs. Irving was able to produce 61 yards on 16 carries, but he failed to find the end zone and wasn't targeted. No Buccaneers pass catcher cleared 37 receiving yards, with top wide receiver Emeka Egbuka limited to 13 yards on four targets.

As feared, Daniels is going to rely heavily on his legs (55 yards on eight carries) and will severely limit the team's passing game (5.5 YPA, 4.2 aDOT). Irving's heavy usage as a ball carrier means he should remain in lineups, but even he is risky -- especially with Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker (both of whom scored in Week 4) also involved. No other Buccaneers players should be near lineups.

Over/under: 47.6 (4th highest)

Win probability: Cowboys 83% (2nd highest)

-->

Philadelphia Eagles @ Jacksonville Jaguars
Projected score: Jaguars 28, Eagles 19

Lineup locks: Trevor Lawrence, Bhayshul Tuten, Parker Washington

Fantasy scoop: Washington should remain in lineups this week despite having now scored fewer fantasy points in each consecutive week of the season -- the most recent of which was a one-catch, 7-yard showing on three targets against the Bengals on Sunday. Still, there's not much need to panic here. For starters, Washington did score 13-plus fantasy points in each of his first three games and his playing time hasn't wavered (75% snap share, 85% route participation on the season). Additionally, Sunday's dud can at least partially be attributed to shadow coverage by standout corner DJ Turner on all 12 of Washington's perimeter routes.

Washington's target share remains strong at 26% and he remains a WR2 against an Eagles defense that has allowed 19-plus fantasy points to three receivers during its last two outings.

Over/under: 46.7 (5th highest)

Win probability: Jaguars 80% (3rd highest)

Chicago Bears @ Green Bay Packers
Projected score: Bears 24, Packers 20

Lineup locks: D'Andre Swift, Matthew Golden, Christian Watson, Luther Burden III

Fantasy scoop: Kyle Monangai exploded for 146 yards and two touchdowns on 30 carries against the Jets on Sunday. Monangai's career day was inflated by Chicago outsnapping New York 89-32 (regression alert!), but it's notable that the second-year back outsnapped Swift 48-32. Despite the strong effort, we can't get too carried away here, as he trailed Swift in snaps (134-75), carries (54-30) and targets (10-4) during the first three games of the season.

Monangai, who had exactly 10 carries through the first three games of the season, very well could take on a larger share of the workload moving forward, but the more likely outcome is that his usage will be inconsistent, just like in 2025. Additionally, his fantasy output remains limited by a minimal receiving role (five targets in four games).

Monangai, who has two games with 20-plus fantasy points and two with less than 8.0 points this season, is running the ball well (5.4 YPC) behind a terrific line, but he won't always be the hot hand. He's no more than a boom/bust flex in a good matchup against a Green Bay defense that has allowed the second-most TDs (eight) and third-most fantasy points to RBs.

Over/under: 44.1 (10th highest)

Win probability: Bears 65% (5th highest)

Houston Texans @ Tennessee Titans
Projected score: Texans 21, Titans 18

Lineup locks: Nico Collins, Carnell Tate

Fantasy scoop: C.J. Stroud came through with 347 passing yards and a pair of touchdowns against Dallas in Week 4. The 23.1 fantasy point effort was his fourth best showing over his last 39 games, tracing back to the start of the 2024 season. Stroud's passing production has been good (top eight in attempts, completions and yards), but that's been inflated by game script -- Houston has trailed on 71% of its offensive snaps, fourth highest -- and he's thrown only five TD passes (19th).

Stroud remains a minimal factor as a rusher (9-66-0 on the season) and won't be a recommended streaming option anytime soon. That includes against a Titans defense yet to allow 19 fantasy points to any quarterback this season.

Over/under: 39.3 (Lowest)

Win probability: Texans 61% (7th highest)

Cincinnati Bengals @ Miami Dolphins
Projected score: Bengals 27, Dolphins 17

Lineup locks: Joe Burrow, Chase Brown, Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins

Fantasy scoop: In the Dolphins' first game without De'Von Achane, their RB usage was as follows: Ollie Gordon II had 22 snaps, nine carries, nine routes and two targets while Jaylen Wright saw 11 snaps, five carries, two routes and zero targets. Interestingly, Wright drew the start and played the first three snaps, but it was Gordon who emerged as the hot hand. The 2025 sixth-round pick showed well with a 9-100-1 rushing line -- and that came despite Miami managing only 37 offensive snaps (the league average this season is 61.8). Gordon was also productive in Week 3 (55 yards and one score on 20 touches), so it's very possible he'll be able to hang in there in the flex conversation. However, there's obvious risk with Wright in the mix on a low-scoring offense.

Over/under: 43.3 (11th highest)

Win probability: Bengals 83% (Highest)

Las Vegas Raiders @ New England Patriots
Projected score: Patriots 23, Raiders 21

Lineup locks: Ashton Jeanty, Brock Bowers

Fantasy scoop: In Week 4, Romeo Doubs exploded for six catches, 58 yards and a pair of touchdowns on a season-high nine targets. The performance came after the ex-Packer totaled a 6-145-0 receiving line on just 11 targets during his first three games. Doubs' playing time has been consistent throughout the season, but the big change in Week 4 (which also applies to Drake Maye) was the opposition. After facing Seattle (second in defensive EPA), Pittsburgh (13th) and Jacksonville (fourth) during Weeks 1-3, the Patriots' passing game took a big leap forward against Buffalo (28th) on Sunday.

This week, New England will face a surprisingly solid Las Vegas defense (seventh) that has allowed a league-low 49% catch rate to receivers this season. Tyquan Thornton and Chris Olave have produced 19-plus points against Las Vegas over the past two weeks, so there's some hope here, but we shouldn't get too carried away with Doubs just yet. He should be valued as a WR3/flex until A.J. Brown returns in a few weeks.

Over/under: 44.4 (9th highest)

Win probability: Patriots 58% (9th highest)

Minnesota Vikings @ New Orleans Saints
Projected score: Vikings 24, Saints 21

Lineup locks: Aaron Jones Sr., Justin Jefferson, Chris Olave

Fantasy scoop: On Monday, in the Saints' first game with Travis Etienne Jr. on IR, their RB usage was as follows: Alvin Kamara had 28 snaps, seven carries, 18 routes and seven targets; Kendre Miller saw 18 snaps, six carries, 10 routes and three targets; CJ Donaldson got 24 snaps, three carries, 13 routes and two targets. Kamara was limited to 23 rushing yards but scored two touchdowns and posted a healthy 5-35-0 receiving line. Miller and Donaldson, meanwhile, combined for 42 scrimmage yards and zero touchdowns on 13 touches.

Kamara's usage, which would have been slightly higher in a more competitive game, is enough to keep him in the flex discussion, but his ceiling is limited with the team committed to rotating between three backs. Kamara is best avoided this week against a Minnesota defense that has allowed only one touchdown and the fewest fantasy points to RBs.

Over/under: 44.6 (8th highest)

Win probability: Vikings 61% (8th highest)

Cleveland Browns @ New York Jets
Projected score: Jets 22, Browns 20

Lineup locks: Quinshon Judkins, Garrett Wilson

Fantasy scoop: Deshaun Watson sits 13th among quarterbacks in fantasy points this season, which is higher than you might think for a guy yet to deliver a top-10 fantasy week. Watson has been more solid than spectacular, having yet to clear 268 passing yards in any game and with a total of just six TDs through four outings. Watson has made up for that with his legs, ranking in the top three among QBs in both carries (31) and rushing yards (127).

Watson has found his way to the QB2 mix, but he's an uninspiring Week 5 start against a Jets defense that has allowed the fifth-fewest QB fantasy points. Granted, the competition has been fairly light, but no QB has reached 20 points against New York this season.

Over/under: 42.4 (13th highest)

Win probability: Jets 56% (11th highest)

Indianapolis Colts @ Pittsburgh Steelers
Projected score: Steelers 22, Colts 21

Lineup locks: Jonathan Taylor, Jaylen Warren, DK Metcalf, Josh Downs, Tyler Warren

Fantasy scoop: Michael Pittman Jr. has scored a total of 15.9 fantasy points in three games with the Steelers this season. This, after the veteran receiver hit that mark in six individual games with the Colts last season. Pittman has been on the field plenty (78% snap share, 72% route participation) but simply hasn't been on Aaron Rodgers' radar very often. Pittman's 11.1% target share is less than half of his 25.3% rate during the past five seasons. He's also yet to clear five targets in any game and has a total of just 31 yards on nine targets since returning from injury in Week 3.

Pittman might eventually emerge as a flex option, but the minuscule usage means -- at least for the time being -- he belongs on benches (or, in shallower leagues, left on the waiver wire).

Over/under: 43.3 (12th highest)

Win probability: Steelers 54% (13th highest)

New York Giants @ Washington Commanders
Projected score: Commanders 23, Giants 22

Lineup locks: Jayden Daniels, Malik Nabers, Terry McLaurin, Isaiah Likely

Fantasy scoop: Cam Skattebo has been busy to open the 2026 season, but it hasn't converted to much fantasy upside. The second-year back has played on a healthy 65% of the Giants' offensive snaps and sits 10th among backs in carries and 18th in scrimmage yards. Skattebo has been limited by underwhelming rushing production (3.46 YPC), a lack of scoring (one TD, two carries inside the 5) and a minimal role in the passing game (67 yards on nine targets).

Skattebo is averaging 11.1 fantasy PPG and has yet to deliver a top-15 fantasy week. The rushing workload is just enough to keep Skattebo in the RB2 mix against a Washington defense that has allowed the fourth-fewest RB fantasy points (only Jonathan Taylor has reached 11 points against them).

Over/under: 44.8 (7th highest)

Win probability: Commanders 56% (10th highest)

Denver Broncos @ Los Angeles Chargers
Projected score: Broncos 21, Chargers 20

Lineup locks: None

Fantasy scoop: RJ Harvey's involvement in the Denver passing game reached a new high Sunday when the second-year back caught all 10 of his targets for 68 yards against the 49ers. Harvey previously posted 4-23-0 and 6-41-0 receiving lines in his first two appearances of the season and, despite missing Week 2, sits top 6 among running backs in targets, catches and receiving yards.

Generally, that amount of receiving workload would get a running back into the RB2 mix, but Harvey has been a near-zero as a rusher (12-49-0). With J.K. Dobbins handling most of the carries and Tyler Badie also a factor in the passing game, Harvey remains a low-ceiling flex option, at best.

Over/under: 41.1 (14th highest)

Win probability: Broncos 52% (14th highest)

Detroit Lions @ Arizona Cardinals
Projected score: Lions 31, Cardinals 28

Lineup locks: Jared Goff, Jacoby Brissett, Jahmyr Gibbs, Jeremiyah Love, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Michael Wilson, Trey McBride, Sam LaPorta

Fantasy scoop: Both Goff and Brissett are streaming options this week against two defenses that have struggled badly against the pass. Goff will face an Arizona defense that has allowed 11 passing TDs and a 9.1 YPA (both highest in the league), whereas Brissett is in an even better spot against a Detroit unit that is worst in defensive EPA and has allowed the most yards, TDs and fantasy points to QBs. Bryce Young's 21.4 fantasy points in Week 4 was the worst showing by a QB against Detroit through four games.

Goff (19-plus fantasy points in three straight games) is the safer play of the two, but Brissett (31 total TDs in 16 games since taking over as Arizona's starter) isn't far behind.

Over/under: 58.4 (Highest)

Win probability: Lions 62% (6th highest)

San Francisco 49ers @ Seattle Seahawks
Projected score: Seahawks 24, 49ers 24

Lineup locks: Christian McCaffrey, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Mike Evans, George Kittle

Fantasy scoop: On Sunday, Emanuel Wilson took control (for now) of the Seattle backfield, totaling a 21-81-1 rushing line and adding 3-39-1 on four targets. His big game came with Jadarian Price on IR, though Wilson has now handled over half of the team's carries in three consecutive games, including a 21-carry, 92-yard effort in Week 2. Wilson is eventually going to cede work to the likes of Zach Charbonnet (seemingly a couple weeks away from a return) and perhaps also Price, but he appears likely to remain the feature back in Week 5.

Wilson is in a respectable spot against a 49ers defense that has allowed the eighth-most RB fantasy points, including 19-plus to Jeremiyah Love and RJ Harvey over the past two weeks.

Over/under: 47.9 (3rd highest)

Win probability: Seahawks 51% (Lowest)

Baltimore Ravens @ Atlanta Falcons
Projected score: Falcons 25, Ravens 20

Lineup locks: Bijan Robinson, Derrick Henry, Drake London, Zay Flowers

Fantasy scoop: With Lamar Jackson in doubt for Week 5, Tyler Huntley will be under center for the Ravens. In the 17 career games in which he's played on 80% or more of snaps, Huntley has a total of 17 touchdowns (12 passing, 5 rushing) and 11 interceptions. He's averaging 177.6 passing yards and 14.0 fantasy PPG during those outings, with a lot of his production coming via the run (7.8 carries and 41.9 rushing yards per game).

Two of those 17 games came during the 2025 season, where both Henry (32.4 fantasy PPG) and Flowers (13.6) remained good fantasy options. Those two belong in lineups against Atlanta, though fringe starters such as Mark Andrews are best left on benches.

Over/under: 45.1 (6th highest)

Win probability: Falcons 54% (12th highest)

Buffalo Bills @ Los Angeles Rams
Projected score: Rams 30, Bills 25

Lineup locks: Josh Allen, Kyren Williams, James Cook III, Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, DJ Moore

Fantasy scoop: The Dalton Kincaid train has come to a screeching halt. The fourth-year tight end appeared to be on the verge of a breakout season after posting receiving lines of 5-130-0 and 7-95-1 during the first two games of the season. However, in the two games since, he has totaled a 3-45-0 line on only five targets. After seeing his most playing time since midway through the 2024 season in Week 1, Kincaid has had his snap share and route participation progressively dip each of the past three weeks.

Kincaid's track record suggests boom/bust playing time and fantasy production is what we should continue to expect from him -- and that makes him a risky play against the Rams on Monday night. Los Angeles has allowed the fewest yards (85) to tight ends this season and none have cleared 8.3 fantasy points.

Over/under: 55 (2nd highest)

Win probability: Rams 70% (4th highest)

stories.headline: Arsenal 'very lucky' Mikel Arteta signed new deal, he is the 'best' - Declan Rice
stories.summary: Declan Rice has said that Arsenal are "very lucky" to have the "best" coach in Mikel Arteta after the Spaniard signed a four-year contract, committing his future at the club.
stories.body:
Declan Rice has said that Arsenal are "very lucky" to have the "best" coach in Mikel Arteta after the Spaniard signed a four-year contract to commit his future at the club.

Arteta has been in charge of the north London side since 2019, making him the longest-serving manager in England's top four leagues and will remain at Arsenal until 2030.

- Mikel Arteta signs new four-year Arsenal contract

In an exclusive interview with ESPN Brazil, Rice lauded the impact Arteta has had on Arsenal, having guided the Gunners to their first Premier League title in 22 years last season.

"It's just tactically, training, managing, the detail he goes into, the things he sees that you would never see," Rice told Renato Senise. "He's constantly watching you when you don't think you're being watched.

"He's watching, constantly asking questions to try and catch you out, to see if you're listening. He's always keeping you on your toes, making sure that you're ready.

"Every time we go into games, tactically we know what we're doing. Defensively, with the ball, how we're going to beat the opposition. It's just the fine details, the way he breaks everything down, which makes him the best for me.

"It's amazing that he [Arteta] signed a new contract and we get to have him as our manager for the next four years. So, we'll be very lucky."

Rice has started every game for Arsenal this season but withdrew from England duty during the international break to manage his workload.

The 27-year-old midfielder provided the positive update that he feels ready to play when the Premier League resumes this weekend.

"It's probably the first time, maybe the second time that I've ever missed a camp since I made my debut for England so I was gutted to miss the camp, but after an honest conversation with Thomas [Tuchel] and the boss here, it was the best thing for me to do, to settle down some of the issues that I've had," Rice said.

"And now I feel good, I feel fresh, and going into this next set of games, I'm going to feel really good."

- Viktor Gyökeres has shone for Sweden. Can he do it for Arsenal now?

- Premier League team news, injury updates after international break

- Arsenal's Mikel Arteta: Premier League still best in the world despite Man City guilty verdict

Asked if the players felt different returning to the pitch this season as reigning champions, Rice insisted their title-winning campaign is in the past and they must focus on new challenges.

"It [winning the league] was an amazing achievement, but this year's a brand new season: New team, new opposition, new players. So it throws up a different challenge," Rice said. "So, yeah, OK, we are the champions, but we don't go on the pitch and think about last season.

"We're definitely playing with more confidence this season, you can feel that within the group, but it's about staying humble, and taking each game as it comes like we did last year and trying to win as many as possible."

Arsenal host Leeds United on Saturday and will be looking to bounce back from a 3-0 defeat to Brighton to put their title defence back on track.

stories.headline: 2026 MLB playoffs: October MVP tracker
stories.summary: We go inside the numbers on the players doing the most to help their teams win.
stories.body:
Who is hero of the 2026 MLB playoffs?

To try to answer to that question, we're tabulating the cumulative win probability added figures for every player in the postseason. But we've added a twist: The deeper we get into the playoffs, the more weight the WPA carries. The division series counts double the wild-card round, then we'll double it again for the championship series and, finally, once again for the World Series.

This means that players who shine in the early rounds can still get on the leaderboard, but it's more difficult. Coming through when the championship leverage is at its highest is what becoming an October hero is all about.

Thursday's hero: A perennial MVP candidate, Jose Ramirez struggled through an injury-plagued regular season at the plate. In two games at Chicago, Ramirez declared those struggles to be behind him, all but carrying the Guardians to a pair of season-saving wins.

Methodology
As mentioned above, each player's win probability added (WPA) is tracked on a per-game basis. Each round of the playoffs counts double that of the previous round. The tabulation is then converted to an AXE-style index in which 100 represents the average for all postseason players. The "Change" column looks in the changes in AXE numbers from the previous day for players who were in action. You can sort this column by clicking on it to see the day's heroes.
